entries.claim: Task 2's all-surface verification is not failure-capable for multiline invocations: it considers only a physical line containing both `planning.mjs` and `risk-check run`, then expects the range flags on that same line.
entries.failure_scenario: A workflow can split `planning.mjs`, `risk-check run`, and its flags across continuation lines—or leave an invalid invocation in that form. The candidate set omits it, so the JavaScript assertion passes vacuously; the grep pipeline also exits successfully when an unfiltered violation is printed. RNG-05's tree-wide no-invalid-revision invariant can therefore remain false under the prescribed verification.

counter_evidence.note: every risk-check run invocation line in the tree is one physical line today (risk-surface.md:14, execute.md:339, task.md:155, execute-parallel.md:34), so the multiline arm has no site to pass vacuously on; a hardening, not a false verification

entries.claim: RSK-10 is not fully delivered because the plan knowingly leaves `references/execute-parallel.md` emitting the same self-comparing range that Task 3 removes from sequential execution.
entries.failure_scenario: A parallel plan lands no commits, merges back without moving HEAD, and then runs the documented check with equal base and head. The seam writes `checked:true, empty:true` rather than `risk_check_skipped`, directly violating the requirement that a plan landing no commits produce no such clean row and the phase goal that no caller hand the blocking check an inapplicable range.

entries.claim: Task 3 adds two prose `trace append` producer sites but neither the task nor PLAN-2's frontmatter declares `cadence-core/bin/trace.test.mjs`, the stated holder of the affected trace-producer census.
entries.failure_scenario: Adding the `risk_check_skipped` invocations changes the census parsed and pinned by `trace.test.mjs`. Merely running that test cannot re-pin it; the test fails or the plan-time/commit lease rejects the undeclared edit. PLAN-1's separate declaration does not authorize PLAN-2, which is explicitly sequential and has a disjoint lease.

counter_evidence.note: the producer census at :3283-3330 asserts --family is in FAMILIES and checks lifecycle event names only; the BRACKETING map at :3201 counts trace close sites, not append lines; the census registered with holder trace.test.mjs (census-registry.mjs:141-149, trace-refusal-sentences) has subjects bin/planning.mjs and bin/planning/, not workflow prose; lease-check --phase 1 --plan 2 --plan-time answers ok:true without it. Task 3 edits nothing in that file.

entries.claim: Task 4 departs from the locked OQ-1 decision to support staged `risk-check status`: it leaves receipts ref-only and knowingly makes every matched staged record remain `unfired`, while verifying only the clean-record case.
entries.failure_scenario: A staged authentication fix produces non-empty matches and receives the required blocking review. Because the staged range has no head commit and no receipt spelling can name it, `risk-check status --base HEAD --staged` can never recognize that fire and continues to refuse as `unfired`. Thus the newly accepted staged status form is unusable on the risky cases it exists to gate, despite OQ-1 requiring the status arm to support that scope.

counter_evidence.note: nothing in the tree calls risk-check status with --staged (execute.md:381 and execute-parallel.md:48 pass --base/--head per plan); a plan-less staged record keys to plan "" and is not joined by a per-plan status (:785-787); the OQ-1 answer in ROADMAP names no receipt spelling, so task 4 departs from nothing locked. The missing settle spelling is real and is the human call the plan Notes already raise.
